D3 は「設定済み catalogue の各 bytes」および「設定済み rustdoc baseline の各 bytes」を完全に fingerprint する open-set の決定を記録していますが、その完全追跡を Cargo・rustdoc・git・ドメイン型など既存 authority に委譲するのか、保守的 over-approximation とするのか、深さ見積り付きの strict implementation とするのかを記録していません。未解決の完全追跡コミットメントになっています。

findings.message: D3 は実装 fingerprint を「保守的 over-approximation」と位置付けていますが、同じ段落で build-script の出力と proc-macro expansion を fingerprint から除外しています。これらは rustdoc JSON に影響し得るため、tracked workspace files・toolchain・metadata が同じでも生成結果が変わり、古い型シグナルを再利用できます。除外を維持するなら over-approximation／安全な再利用という決定を修正する必要があります。

`$PWD` を JSON 文字列へ無加工で埋め込んでいるため、`tempfile::tempdir()` の親パスに `"`、バックスラッシュ、改行などが含まれる環境では shim が不正な Cargo metadata JSON を返し、正常系テストが CLI 境界へ到達する前に失敗します。この一時パスの文字集合前提は spec／環境前提宣言にありません（未宣言の前提への依存）。`serde_json` などで manifest path を正しくエスケープしてください。

`CARGO_HOME` だけを削除すると fingerprint 処理はホストの `$HOME/.cargo/config.toml` または `config` を読みます。そのファイルが symlink、非通常ファイル、過大、または読取不能なら、この成功期待テストは環境依存で失敗します。fixture 専用の一時ディレクトリへ `HOME` も向け、Cargo home の状態をテスト内で固定してください。

`manifest_path.to_string_lossy()` は Unix の非 UTF-8 パスを置換文字へ黙って変更するため、`TMPDIR` などに非 UTF-8 byte が含まれると shim が実在しない manifest path を返し、正常系テストが失敗します。workspace／一時パスを UTF-8 に限定する前提は spec と環境前提宣言のどちらにもありません（未宣言の前提への依存）。lossy 変換を避けるか、UTF-8 制約と失敗動作を契約として宣言してください。

`run_in_dir` はプロセス全体の current directory を変更しますが、`process_env_lock` は同じ mutex を取得するテストしか直列化しません。CLI の同一 unit-test binary には mutex を使わず `tempdir_in(std::env::current_dir())` を呼ぶ batch-plan テストなどがあり、並行するとこの fixture repository 内へ一時ファイルを作成して worktree/fingerprint 判定を不定にできます。これは宣言されていない並行実行前提への依存で、テスト独立性にも反します。プロセス cwd を変更せず metadata path を解決するか、`Command::current_dir` を使う子プロセスへ隔離してください。

正常系 fixture を `tempdir_in("/tmp")` に固定すると、`/tmp` が存在して書込み可能かつ symlink でない Unix 環境を暗黙に要求します。特に macOS では通常 `/tmp` が `/private/tmp` への symlink であり、D7 に従う workspace/target の ancestor symlink guard がこの成功テストを拒否します。この platform/filesystem 前提は spec と環境前提宣言にありません（未宣言の前提への依存）。環境の temp root を canonicalize・検証して使うなど、固定 `/tmp` を避けてください。

`canonicalize()` は path の byte encoding を UTF-8 に変換しないため、`TMPDIR` が有効な非 UTF-8 Unix path の場合は `manifest_path.to_str()` が失敗し、この正常系テストが panic します。canonical temp root が UTF-8 になる前提は spec と環境前提宣言にありません（未宣言の前提への依存）。UTF-8 を要求しない fixture transport にするか、対応 encoding と非 UTF-8 時の動作を契約として宣言してください。

親／子の判定を ambient な `SOTP_TYPE_SIGNALS_CHILD` の存在だけに委ねているため、CI や開発環境で同名変数が既に設定されていると fixture と子プロセスを作らず、通常の repository cwd で子側ロジックを実行してテストが失敗します。この環境変数が未設定という前提は宣言されていません（未宣言の前提への依存）。fixture 固有の nonce/path も検証する marker にしてください。

`current_exe()` を直接再実行する方式は、現在の test binary が OS からネイティブ実行可能であることを要求します。Cargo の target runner/QEMU 経由で Unix target のテストを実行している場合、親は動作してもこの `Command` は runner を経由せず `Exec format error` になります。こうした subprocess/platform 前提は spec と環境前提宣言にありません（未宣言の前提への依存）。runner を迂回する自己再実行を避けて隔離してください。

fixture を `tempdir_in(current_dir)` で作るため、テスト実行ディレクトリが書込み可能であることを暗黙に要求し、read-only source checkout では即座に失敗します。また通常の repository cwd では実行中に未追跡の nested repository を作るため、同じ mutex を取得しない並行テストの worktree-clean 判定や走査結果を汚染できます。この filesystem／並行実行前提は spec と環境前提宣言にありません（未宣言の前提への依存）。共有 source tree 外の隔離領域を使ってください。

fixture を `tempdir_in(current_dir)` で作るため、テスト実行ディレクトリが書込み可能であることを暗黙に要求し、read-only source checkout では失敗します。また repository cwd では実行中に未追跡の nested repository を作り、同じ mutex を取得しない並行テストの worktree-clean 判定や走査結果を汚染します。briefing が要求するとおり、fixture を repository 外の隔離 temp directory に移してください。

isolated fixture を作った後も `root` 自体は canonicalize せず CLI へ渡しているため、`TMPDIR` が symlink を経由する環境では D7 の workspace ancestor symlink guard がこの正常系テストを拒否します。`target_dir` だけでなく fixture workspace と以降の全 path に canonical root を使用してください。

`tempfile::tempdir()` の絶対 path を `to_str()` へ渡しているため、非 UTF-8 の `TMPDIR` では正常系テストが panic します。temporary root が UTF-8 という前提は spec と環境前提宣言にありません（未宣言の前提への依存）。UTF-8 を要求しない fixture transport にするか、対応 encoding と失敗動作を契約化してください。

fixture を固定 `/tmp` 配下に作るため、すべての `cfg(unix)` 環境に `/tmp` が存在して書込み可能という未宣言の platform/filesystem 前提へ依存します。chroot、sandbox、read-only `/tmp` では正常系テストが fixture 作成前に失敗します。環境から得た隔離 temp root を検証して使い、固定 `/tmp` を避けてください。

`/tmp` の canonical path に非 UTF-8 component がある場合、`to_string_lossy()` は manifest path を別の文字列へ変更し、shim が実在しない path を返します。panic を避けても正常系は失敗するため、lossy 変換では encoding 前提を解消できません（未宣言の前提への依存）。実在 path を保持できる transport を使うか、UTF-8 を保証できる root を明示的に選別してください。

Removing `is_placed()` admits every unplaced identity whose rendered string matches, including declarations owned by `catalogue_crate`. For example, with an unplaced local `domain::UserId`, `crate::UserId` normalizes to `domain::UserId` and now resolves successfully even though D3 says qualified local paths require an exact placement and omitted `module_path` must not mean crate root. This weakens fail-closed local resolution in all callers of this shared resolver. Preserve the new match only for cross-crate identities (while retaining placed exact matches), and add a same-crate qualified-path regression test.

`AuthoritativeRustdocContext` claims to bind a graph pair to one layer, but it stores no `LayerId` and performs no consistency check. A caller can insert a context for layer A under layer B in the `BTreeMap`, causing cross-crate resolution to use the wrong rustdoc graphs. Encode the layer identity in the value object or validate the key/value association before use.

The newly added test function does not follow the required `test_{target}_{condition}_{expected_result}` naming convention. Rename `authoritative_context_new_preserves_baseline_and_current_graphs` accordingly.

`ExpectedRustdocJsonPath::try_new` uses lexical `Path::starts_with`, so a path such as `/target/../outside/current.json` is accepted as being inside the target directory. This violates the documented confinement invariant and can make adapters read rustdoc data outside the resolved target directory. Normalize/canonicalize or reject parent traversal before accepting the path.

`RustdocExecutionIdentity::new` accepts `target_directory` and an `ExpectedRustdocJsonPath` independently, without proving that the expected path belongs to the supplied target directory. Callers can construct an identity whose Cargo target is `/a` while its expected JSON path was validated under `/b`, producing an internally inconsistent cache identity. Tie the path to its target directory or validate the relationship in the constructor.

Several newly public APIs lack the required documentation comments (and the fallible free constructors also lack `# Errors` sections): `digest_identity!`-generated `new`/`as_digest` methods for the new digest types, `CapturedRustdocJson::{json_hash,crate_data}`, `RustdocSnapshot::{execution_identity,json_hash,crate_data}`, `RustdocExecutionIdentity::{target_directory,crate_name,features,profile,expected_json_path}`, `TypeSignalsCacheKey::{implementation_fingerprint,resolution_fingerprint,rustdoc_execution_identity}`, `construct_captured_rustdoc_json`, and `construct_rustdoc_snapshot`. Add API docs at each public surface.

`cache_key` hard-codes the new implementation fingerprint, resolution fingerprint, and rustdoc execution identity, so this “each isolated cache identity mismatch” test varies only the pre-existing declaration, HEAD, and baseline fields. The AC-04 reuse contract is therefore untested for all three newly authoritative identities; add isolated mismatch cases proving each one returns `ReextractAndEvaluate`.

The target-directory case is not isolated: `execution_identity_with_selection` joins `doc/domain.json` beneath the changed target, so both `target_directory` and `expected_json_path` differ. This test would still pass if reuse stopped comparing the target directory because the path mismatch alone forces re-extraction. Keep a common valid expected path beneath both target directories so only `target_directory` changes.

This test name puts the expected behavior before the condition, so it does not follow the required `test_{target}_{condition}_{expected_result}` format. Use a name such as `test_rustdoc_execution_identity_components_with_invalid_values_return_errors`.

This test name puts `reextracts` before the condition and therefore does not follow `test_{target}_{condition}_{expected_result}`. Use a name such as `test_decide_type_signals_reuse_with_each_execution_identity_component_changed_reextracts`.

The test name does not follow the required `test_{target}_{condition}_{expected_result}` form, and it combines same-content equality and changed-content inequality without naming either condition/result clearly. Split or rename it to express those cases explicitly.

The test name states an outcome (`preserves_absolute_identity`) but omits the input condition required by `test_{target}_{condition}_{expected_result}`. Rename it to something like `test_resolved_cargo_target_directory_with_absolute_path_preserves_identity`.

`capture_evaluation_start` abstracts runtime acquisition of the workspace, environment, selected tool binaries, and `cargo metadata`. This is an infrastructure capability and its secondary port belongs in usecase; adding it to the domain-owned `RustdocCratePort` makes the innermost layer own an external-boundary operation. Keep the fingerprint value object in domain, but relocate the acquisition port.

`capture_current` validates the supplied evaluation-start fingerprint but returns a `RustdocSnapshot` that contains no fingerprint. A caller can therefore pair a successfully captured snapshot with a different `ImplementationFingerprint` when constructing the cache key, despite the API claiming the snapshot is bound to that fingerprint. Return a value object carrying both the validated fingerprint and snapshot, or otherwise encode that relationship in the successful type.
`construct_attested_rustdoc_snapshot` is a public `Result`-returning API but lacks the required `# Errors` documentation section describing decode failures.

`environment-assumptions.md` explicitly says the template must not provide a default platform, but the new Supported Platforms declaration hard-codes Unix/Linux as the template-wide default. This contradicts the convention's consumer-ownership rule; document the shipped evaluator requirement outside the consumer declaration, or revise the ownership contract consistently.

The Supported Platforms declaration fills in only the OS family (`Unix`, including Linux), while the field explicitly requires platform, architecture, and runtime. State the supported architecture(s) and runtime (or explicitly declare them architecture/runtime-independent) so consumers do not have to infer part of the evaluator contract.

`ci-container` remains a dependency-only task, so `cargo make ci-container` bypasses the new `gate-output` full-log/compact-summary contract applied to the other CI entrypoints. Invoke `gate-output` around `cargo make --allow-private ci-local-steps` here, as done for `ci-rust-container` and `ci-track-container`.

`ci-container` remains dependency-only, so `cargo make ci-container` bypasses the new `gate-output` full-log/compact-summary contract used by the other CI entrypoints. Wrap `cargo make --allow-private ci-local-steps` with `gate-output`, as done for the sibling container tasks.

The conflict resolution drops the type-signals evaluator’s explicit architecture declaration. Here, `x86_64` qualifies only gate-log persistence; the type-signals clause specifies Unix and its runtime constraints but no architecture. Since this field requires platform, architecture, and runtime, readers must infer whether type-signals is CPU-independent or x86_64-only. Restore the prior architecture-independent wording while retaining the gate-log declaration.

The ownership rules say declaration fields are consumer-owned and carve out only the type-signals Supported Platforms contract, but the document now places fixed gate-log platform behavior and the shipped `gate-output` resource contract in those fields. Extend the framework-owned exception to these shipped-component contracts or move them out of the consumer declaration.

The resource declaration omits the adapter's actual memory behavior. `ProcessGateRunner` uses `Command::output()` to buffer both streams in memory and then `combine_output` allocates a combined copy before persistence. With no byte cap, memory is unbounded and OOM can terminate the process before any full log or `GateLogWriteOutcome::Unavailable` is produced; the stated time/disk replacement boundaries do not cover this. Declare the in-memory bound and failure behavior or introduce bounded/streamed capture.

The statement that caller-side `cargo make` enforces the processing-time limit is false for the scoped Makefile entrypoints: they invoke `gate-output` directly without a timeout, and cargo-make itself supplies no deadline. Consequently a non-terminating child can wait indefinitely in local `cargo make` use, contrary to the claim that an upper boundary will terminate it. State that only callers which explicitly provide a timeout impose one, or add such a boundary.

This now says the template commonly documents the fixed gate-log and `gate-output` contracts, but the file’s own preamble and `template-boundary.json` establish that source `knowledge/conventions/` is replaced by the export overlay. The exported `environment-assumptions.md` still leaves both Supported Platforms and Resource Limits as consumer TODOs, and the included documentation only carries the type-signals Unix bound. Fresh consumers therefore do not receive the gate-log platform or `gate-output` resource contracts claimed here. Put those framework-owned contracts on an included distribution surface or seed them into the exported overlay consistently.

記録済み結果の再利用判定に渡す `current_key` は target catalogue hash・HEAD・target baseline hash の3項目だけである。実装 fingerprint と解決 fingerprint は現在の呼び出し中に変化しなかったことしか確認されず、記録値とは比較されない。そのため clean worktree のまま `RUSTFLAGS` や `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` が変わって rustdoc graph が変化しても、`SkipEvaluation` が古い signal を成功として再利用する。D3 / AC-04 が列挙する実装・解決・resolved target・crate/features/profile・expected JSON path を永続化キーへ含めて比較すること。

`rustdoc_input_fingerprint` は workspace の走査と環境値 allowlist だけで fingerprint を作り、Cargo metadata、workspace 外の path dependency、build script の外部入力・生成物、または識別不能な toolchain / CARGO_HOME 内容を検出して拒否しない。例えば `path = "../shared"` の依存元が変わっても repository は clean、fingerprint も同一なので、古い signal/context を再利用できる。AC-04 / CO-04 のとおり authoritative input set を完全に確定できない構成は export 前に fail-closed にすること。

evaluator は承認済み type contract が sole rustdoc construction boundary とする `RustdocCratePort` / `RustdocCrateAdapter` を使わず、`RustdocSchemaExporter` を直接構築して infrastructure-local provider へ渡している。この経路では resolved target、crate/features/profile、expected path、bytes digest を束縛した identity-bearing snapshot を受け取れず、Architecture Verification Checklist の「Ports implemented, not bypassed」と D3/D8 を満たさない。rustdoc I/O を承認済み port/adapter 境界へ一本化すること。

期待 JSON path と target directory を lock 取得前に解決し、通常の共有 Cargo target directory 上でこの provider だけが advisory lock に参加している。既存 exporter や外部 `cargo rustdoc` の参加、または target directory の専用所有を検証しないため、別 writer が JSON を置換しても完全な `String` として authoritative に受理できる。CO-06/CO-07/AC-06 が要求する専用所有・全 writer 参加・同一臨界区間での path 決定から bytes snapshot までを実装し、確認不能なら fail-closed にすること。

評価開始時の fingerprint と、後から再読した path の終了時 fingerprint を比較するだけで、実際に評価する他層 catalogue/baseline/source bytes は開始 snapshot に束縛されていない。入力が A で開始した後、再読時に B へ変わって評価へ入り、終了確認前に A へ戻ると start/end hash は一致し、B 由来の結果を永続化できる。`BaselineSnapshot` も path+hash の再読だけで同じ ABA 問題を持つ。D8/IN-07どおり、解決済み content-addressed immutable snapshots の同じ bytes だけを評価へ渡すこと。

追加された唯一の property-style test は codec だけを実行し、現在の `test-bindings.json` にも登録されていない。変更された evaluator/adapter には、完全な再利用キー、外部入力拒否、65層目、writer ownership、入力/output ABA を生成状態で検証する property-based test がない。Testing Convention に従い evaluator の property evidence を追加し、この codec property とともに該当 obligation へ binding すること。

`RustdocCrateAdapter::load_from_path` は `workspace_root` を trusted root として渡していますが、`read_optional_regular_file_bytes` の non-Linux 実装では trusted-root 検証が no-op です。さらに `reject_symlinks_below` は指定 root の配下であること自体を検証しないため、Windows 等では symlink でない workspace 外の任意の baseline path を読み込めます。全プラットフォームで canonical path または opened-file の所属が trusted root 配下であることを fail-closed に検証してください。

lock 取得時に安全に開いた target-directory descriptor を保持せず、`read_bytes` は `target_dir` の文字列 path を再度開き直している。lock 取得後に target directory を rename して同名の実 directory を作ると、lock は旧 directory の inode に残る一方、snapshot は新 directory から読まれる。別 writer も新しい lock file を取得できるため排他が分裂する。directory handle と inode generation を `RustdocOutputLock` に保持し、全 output をその descriptor から `openat` すること。

rustdoc capture は通常の resolved Cargo target directory をそのまま使用し、機能専用領域の所有や非協調 writer の排除を確認していない。外部の通常の `cargo rustdoc` は advisory lock を無視して同じ `target/doc/<crate>.json` を別 feature で上書きでき、その完全な JSON が requested identity の snapshot として受理される。CO-06/CO-07/AC-06どおり専用 target 領域を確保するか、非協調 writer を検出できなければ fail-closed にすること。

公開された `export_rustdoc_json_path*` は export 中だけ lock を保持し、path を返す時点で lock を解放する。ドキュメントも caller に後続 read を委ねているため、別の協調 writer が read 前に同じ JSON を置換できる。`existing_rustdoc_json_path` も unlocked snapshot reuse を公開している。D8 の immutable snapshot 境界を保つため、これらを bytes/snapshot 返却へ変更するか非公開化すること。

`RUSTC` / `RUSTDOC` / wrapper path は absolute の場合でも lexical `starts_with` しか検査せず、relative value は無条件に許可される。例えば `/workspace/../outside/wrapper` は検査を通って workspace 外の未 fingerprint binary を実行でき、bare command も同じ `PATH` 文字列のまま内容だけ交換できる。正規化・実体解決後に trusted workspace 内へ閉じ、内容を fingerprint できない tool は AC-04 に従って拒否すること。

Cargo input fingerprint は workspace と Cargo home の config だけを読み、Cargo が workspace の親 directory から読む `.cargo/config.toml` を fingerprint も拒否もしていない。また `CARGO_HOME` 未設定時は allowlist 外の `HOME` から path を導出するが、その resolved path 自体を canonical encoding に含めない。親 config や HOME を切り替えて `build.rustflags` 等を変えても同一 fingerprint で古い signal を再利用できる。Cargo の完全な config hierarchy を identity に含めるか、外部 config を fail-closed にすること。

既存 baseline の idempotent path が `std::fs::read_to_string` でファイル全体を無制限に読み込む。rustdoc JSON には他経路で 64 MiB 上限があるのに、この分岐だけ任意サイズを allocation でき、巨大な track artifact で process memory を枯渇させられる。同じ bounded no-follow reader と上限を使用すること。

domain-port 側の baseline capture でも、既存 baseline を `std::fs::read_to_string` で無制限に読むため、巨大な artifact が bounded rustdoc capture を迂回して memory exhaustion を起こせる。64 MiB の bounded regular-file readerを使用して typed I/O errorへ変換すること。

exclusive-lock の property として binding されたこのテストは、単一 lock を取得して静的ファイルを一度読むだけである。第二 writer の排他、120秒 timeout、target ancestor の rename/replacement、非協調 writer の検出を一つも検証せず、現在の lock-generation 欠陥も通過する。Testing Convention と briefing の契約どおり、競合状態と target-generation を生成する property testを追加すること。

codec の generated-state property test は現在も `test-bindings.json` のどの obligation にも登録されていない。Testing Convention は codec property evidence を対象契約へ binding することを要求しているため、該当する codec contract/AC-02 obligationへこのテストを追加すること。

実際の export は `Command::new("cargo")` と `rustup +nightly` が選ぶ外部 toolchain を使うが、内容 hash を追加するのは明示的な `RUSTC` / `RUSTDOC` / wrapper だけである。`RUSTUP_HOME` も identity に含まれないため、同じ `PATH` / `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN` 文字列のまま cargo shim や nightly toolchain が更新されても implementation fingerprint は一致し、旧 signal を再利用できる。実際に使用する cargo・rustup・nightly rustc/rustdoc を解決して内容/generationを fingerprintするか、完全に識別できなければAC-04どおりfail-closedにすること。

version 5 の cache identity に必須フィールドを追加したにもかかわらず、`implementation_fingerprint`、`resolution_fingerprint`、`rustdoc_execution_identity` を `serde(default)` で補完している。旧version-5 artifactが完全なcache keyを持つ文書としてdecodeされ、fabricated zero digestと`/tmp/.../legacy` identityがdomainへ渡るため、versioned schemaがmissing authoritative fieldsをfail-closedに拒否していない。schema versionを更新してこれらを必須化するか、欠落時にcodec errorを返すこと。

このlegacy baseline capture APIは従来default features付きでrustdocを実行していたが、現在は`capture_rustdoc_json(..., &[])`のDeclared modeを呼ぶため、`--no-default-features`が付与される。default featureが公開型を追加するcrateでは、既存のbaseline captureがその型を欠落させ、後続signal判定を誤らせる。feature引数を持たないこの経路はLegacy modeのimmutable-byte APIを使い、従来のdefault-feature semanticsを維持すること。

`resolve_bare_tool` は PATH candidate を `symlink_metadata()` で調べ、regular file の場合だけ採用するため、標準的な rustup installation の `~/.cargo/bin/cargo -> rustup` symlink を無視する。その直後の処理は candidate を canonicalize して実体 bytes を fingerprint できる設計なのに到達せず、通常の rustup 環境で implementation fingerprint と全 type-signal evaluation が `bare tool path was not found` で停止する。PATH symlink は canonicalize 後の実体を no-follow/regular-file検証して fingerprint すること。

`cargo metadata --no-deps` only describes workspace packages, not the resolved dependency closure that `cargo rustdoc` builds. The build-script check below therefore misses build scripts in path or registry dependencies; their untracked inputs/generated outputs can change rustdoc while the implementation fingerprint remains unchanged, allowing stale `SkipEvaluation` reuse contrary to D3/D4 and AC-04. Resolve and validate the selected rustdoc target's complete locked dependency graph, or otherwise attest every build-script input/output.

`append_actual_rustdoc_tool_identity` hashes the PATH-resolved shims rather than the binaries selected by `cargo +nightly`. In a normal rustup installation, `cargo`, `rustc`, and `rustdoc` all canonicalize to the `rustup` executable, while the actual nightly binaries live under `RUSTUP_HOME/toolchains`. Updating the nightly toolchain can therefore change rustdoc output without changing this fingerprint, allowing stale reuse on a clean worktree. Resolve and snapshot the exact nightly cargo/rustc/rustdoc binaries, or fail closed if they cannot be identified.

`cargo metadata --no-deps` returns only workspace members, so the subsequent build-script validation never examines dependency packages that `cargo rustdoc` may compile. A path or registry dependency's build script can consume untracked inputs or generate different output while the implementation fingerprint remains unchanged, allowing stale `SkipEvaluation` reuse contrary to D3/D4 and AC-04. Validate the selected rustdoc target's complete locked dependency closure or otherwise attest every build-script input and output.

`encode_with_workspace` persists the execution-identity paths relative to the real workspace, but `decode` rebases those paths to the fixed `/sotp-workspace` prefix. The evaluator then compares this decoded cache key with a current key containing the checkout's actual absolute target paths, so identical clean runs can never satisfy cache-key equality and always re-extract. Decode relative identities against the current workspace (or compare a path-independent canonical representation on both sides).

`relativize_workspace_path` falls back to serializing the raw absolute path whenever the resolved target lies outside the workspace. Absolute external `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` is explicitly supported, so a valid setting such as `/home/alice/.cache/cargo-target` will still place a work-machine home path in the tracked type-signals JSON, contrary to the stated portability contract. Encode supported external targets with a portable identity (for example, a stable marker plus digest) or fail closed instead of persisting the host path.

The new invalid-identity coverage exercises only two fixed mutations (`expected_json_path` and `profile`). The Testing Convention requires property-based codec coverage for generated boundary and invalid representations; generate semantic-invalid cases across the persisted identity components and verify each maps to `InvalidExecutionIdentity`.

The new name places the expected result (`rejects`) before the condition, contrary to the required `test_{target}_{condition}_{expected_result}` form. Rename it to put the invalid-identity condition before the expected error result.

The generated invalid-identity property omits `target_directory`, even though AC-04 includes the resolved Cargo target directory and this is the identity’s trusted-root-sensitive path component. Add generated malformed/traversing target-directory representations and verify decoding fails closed with `InvalidExecutionIdentity`.

The newly named fixed test and the new property test are not bound to the relevant obligations: the current bindings still reference the removed `test_decode_rejects_invalid_rustdoc_execution_identity` name. Consequently IN-03/AC-04 point to a nonexistent test and the property evidence is unbound; update the bindings to reference the new property test.

`workspace_input_fingerprint` is not authoritative: it hashes only four root-level paths and silently omits unreadable/missing files. Changes to workspace-member sources or other Cargo rustdoc inputs can occur during capture without changing this fingerprint, allowing an inconsistent snapshot to be accepted. Use the complete bounded authoritative input fingerprint and fail closed on every I/O/coverage error.

The start/end guard hashes only path names and file bytes, so an input can change A→B→A during rustdoc capture and compare equal. This violates the required no-ABA guarantee; include generation metadata in the capture consistency check or otherwise use the repository’s generation-aware authoritative fingerprint.

`未宣言の前提への依存`: 開始・終了 fingerprint は `PATH`、`RUSTDOCFLAGS` 等の process environment の現在値を再読するだけです。rustdoc 起動時だけ A→B、その後 A に戻ると両 fingerprint は一致し、B の環境で生成した snapshot を A の identity として受理します。AC-06 の no-ABA 契約を満たすには、取得した環境 snapshot を全 Cargo/rustdoc subprocess に固定するか、実行中の環境不変性を正式に宣言・強制してください。

`rustdoc_input_fingerprint` の I/O、symlink、resource-limit failure と fingerprint mismatch がすべて `CaptureFailed` に変換されます。呼び出し側はこれを `EvaluateSignalsError::Evaluation` とするため、types/spec が要求する authoritative-input failure と rustdoc/lock failure の区別が失われます。authoritative-input failure を保持できる typed variantを追加して伝搬してください。

no-retry テストは `acquire_for_test` をテスト自身が二回呼ぶだけで、単一の取得処理内の試行回数を観測していません。adapter 側のテストも `capture()` を二回呼ぶ同じ構造なので、実装が各呼び出しで内部 retry してから失敗しても通過します。retry が仕様対象であるため、recording seam等で一回の capture における lock-operation attempt が一回だけであることを検証してください。

no-fallback 用の stale JSON は `target-area/doc/lockfail.json` に置かれていますが、adapter の実際の期待出力は private target の `.sotp-rustdoc/<selection-hash>/doc/lockfail.json` です。この fixture は fallback 候補にならないため、実装が実際の期待 path の既存 JSON を再利用する regression でもテストが失敗を返して通過できます。実際の exclusive target に stale JSON を置いた状態で lock operationだけを失敗させてください。

このテストは `include_str!` とエラー文の存在だけを確認しており、non-Unix 分岐がコンパイルされることも、capture が fail-closed になることも検証しません。Testing Convention は source の部分文字列を挙動の証拠にすることを明示的に禁止しています。対象 platform の compile/behavior testへ置き換えてください。

source 内の token 順序は lock の lifetime を証明しません。たとえば export と read の間に `drop(lock)` を追加しても、検索対象文字列の順序は変わらずこのテストは通過します。Testing Conventionに従い、競合 writerまたは recording boundaryを使って path selectionからbyte readまでlockが実際に保持されることを検証してください。

`未宣言の前提への依存`: 開始・終了 fingerprint は `PATH`、`RUSTDOCFLAGS` などの process environment の現在値を再読するだけです。rustdoc 起動時だけ環境が A→B、その後 A に戻ると両 fingerprint は一致し、B で生成した snapshot を A の identity として受理します。AC-06 の no-ABA 契約を満たすには、取得した環境 snapshot を全 Cargo/rustdoc subprocess に固定するか、実行中の環境不変性を正式に宣言・強制してください。

`rustdoc_input_fingerprint` の I/O、symlink、resource-limit failure と fingerprint mismatch がすべて `CaptureFailed` に変換されます。呼び出し側はこれを `EvaluateSignalsError::Evaluation` とするため、types/spec が要求する authoritative-input failure と rustdoc/lock failure の区別が失われます。typed な区別を adapter 境界から保持してください。

このテストは source 内の token 順序しか検査せず、lock の lifetime を証明しません。export と read の間に `drop(lock)` を追加しても検索順序は変わらず通過します。また Testing Convention は `include_str!` と source 文字列検索を挙動の証拠にすることを禁止しています。競合 writer または recording boundary を用いた挙動テストへ置き換えてください。

no-retry テストは `acquire_for_test` をテスト自身が二回呼ぶだけで、単一の取得処理内の試行回数を観測していません。実装が各呼び出しで内部 retry してから失敗しても通過します。retry が明示的な契約なので、recording seam などで一回の capture/acquire における lock-operation attempt が一回だけであることを検証してください。

非 Unix の test build では `temp_env` の唯一の参照が `#[cfg(unix)]` テストと共に除去され、この無条件 import が `unused_imports` になります。crate は workspace の `warnings = "deny"` を継承するため、AC-08 の fail-closed テストへ到達する前にコンパイルが失敗します。import も `#[cfg(unix)]` で限定してください。

非 Unix では `RUSTDOC_OUTPUT_LOCK_TIMEOUT` と `PropertyGenerator` の唯一の利用箇所が `#[cfg(unix)]` で除去されます。その結果、無条件 import は `unused_imports`、generator と methods は `dead_code` となり、`warnings = "deny"` により新しい non-Unix fail-closed テストを含む test build 自体が失敗します。これらの Unix 専用補助要素も `#[cfg(unix)]` で限定してください。

`require_exclusive_rustdoc_target` treats the mere presence of a `.sotp-rustdoc` component anywhere in the path as proof of exclusive ownership. For example, an ordinary target such as `/work/.sotp-rustdoc/project/target` is accepted even though its writers need not participate in `RustdocOutputLock`; the evaluator could then treat their JSON as authoritative. CO-06/CO-07/AC-06 require fail-closed verification of the adapter-owned target boundary. Validate the expected `.sotp-rustdoc/<selection>` structure relative to the resolved Cargo target root, or require an equivalent ownership proof, instead of scanning arbitrary ancestors.

This test uses `include_str!` plus substring/order assertions against `schema_export.rs` as behavioral evidence. The testing convention explicitly forbids source-text assertions; replace it with a recording/fake exporter or another runtime behavioral test.
The newly added property test name does not follow the required `test_{target}_{condition}_{expected_result}` convention.

The added test uses `include_str!` and substring/order assertions against `schema_export.rs` as behavioral evidence. The testing convention explicitly forbids source-text assertions; use a runtime behavioral test instead.
The added test name does not follow the required `test_{target}_{condition}_{expected_result}` convention.

`rustdoc_types` is imported unconditionally, but every reference to it is inside a `#[cfg(unix)]` item. On non-Unix test builds this becomes an unused import, and the workspace's `warnings = "deny"` turns it into a hard compilation error, preventing the explicit non-Unix fail-closed tests from running. Remove this redundant import or guard it with `#[cfg(unix)]`.

`reject_workspace_root` は non-Unix でも通常ディレクトリなら `Ok(())` を返します。`RustdocProvider::execution_identity` は lock を取得せず、この admission 後に identity を返すため、matching cache があると evaluator は non-Unix 用 lock rejection を通らず `SkipEvaluation` で成功できます。これは IN-06／AC-08／OS-05 に反します。identity admission 自体を non-Unix で fail-closed にし、cache-reuse 経路を挙動テストしてください。

`SkipEvaluation` は開始時の implementation/resolution fingerprint と worktree 状態だけで即座に成功し、終了世代を再検証しません。key 取得後に別 writer が入力を A→B→A と更新すると、git は clean、recorded key は開始時 key と一致したままなので古い cache が受理されます。追加された ABA テストは cache-miss の評価経路しか通らず、この再利用経路を覆いません。AC-04／AC-06 に従い、成功を返す直前にも世代を比較してください。

findings.message: このテストは `tempfile::tempdir()` の全 ancestor が symlink でないことを暗黙に仮定しています。`TMPDIR` が symlink 配下の場合、または `/var` などが symlink の Unix 環境では、workspace-root guard が private `.sotp-rustdoc` component より先に失敗します。しかも assertion は一般的な `symlink guard` だけを見るため、意図した component を検証せずテストが通ります（未宣言の前提への依存）。fixture root を canonicalize し、対象 component を示すエラーを確認してください。

findings.message: 追加された trusted-root テスト群は `tempfile::tempdir()` の path をそのまま root に使うため、temp root の ancestor に symlink がある環境では containment／missing-root／non-directory の各分岐へ到達せず、先行する symlink guard error で失敗します。これは spec と環境前提宣言にない temp-path 前提です（同じ問題が lines 478, 497, 577 にもあります）。検証済みの canonical fixture root を共有してください。

findings.message: 4 件の新しい generation テストは `setup_workspace()` が返す ambient temp path をそのまま `workspace_root` に渡します。`TMPDIR` またはその ancestor が symlink の Unix 環境では evaluator が root admission で先に停止し、期待する generation-change 診断まで到達しません（同じ問題が lines 2902, 2941, 2977 にもあります）。temp root が symlink-free という前提は未宣言なので、canonicalized fixture root を使ってください。

`workspace_root` is referenced only inside the `#[cfg(unix)]` block. On non-Unix builds it becomes an unused parameter, and this crate inherits `warnings = "deny"`, so the newly added fail-closed branch—and its non-Unix test—cannot compile. Consume the parameter in the non-Unix branch or rename it compatibly across both configurations.

The new non-Unix rejection makes this unguarded success test call `unwrap()` on `CaptureFailed`; `test_non_cooperative_parent_cargo_target_json_is_not_authoritative` has the same problem at line 823. Gate Unix-success tests and their helpers/imports with `#[cfg(unix)]`, leaving the new rejection test for non-Unix.

If the rejected path is restored before this second check—or the runner rejected a different output path selected by its second metadata resolution—the recheck succeeds and an actual trusted-root rejection is incorrectly mapped to `CaptureFailed`. `run_command_with_bounded_output` continues draining both pipes after `MAX_RUSTUP_WHICH_OUTPUT_BYTES` is exceeded and reports the excess only after the child exits. A chatty or hostile PATH-selected `rustup` can therefore cause unbounded I/O for up to 120 seconds, violating the briefing's bounded-resolution requirement and D4's fail-at-the-limit contract. Terminate the process group as soon as the byte budget is exceeded.

The nightly tool snapshots are not charged against the fingerprint's shared 512 MiB total-byte/file-count budget. A workspace already at the limit can still read three additional tool files of up to 64 MiB each, plus resolution output, even though D4 explicitly applies the aggregate limits to nightly tool resolution and content snapshots. `MAX_CARGO_METADATA_OUTPUT_BYTES` does not bound actual I/O on this path. `run_command_with_bounded_output` retains only the first 16 MiB per stream but continues draining until EOF and reports the overflow only after the child exits. Workspace bytes are charged during directory discovery, but the later file read never reconciles that reservation with the fresh metadata or actual byte length. A file can grow after line 362 and remain stable during lines 174–191; the fingerprint then reads and accepts the larger content while charging only its old size, allowing actual I/O to exceed the 512 MiB aggregate limit. Nightly-resolution output is charged to `FingerprintBudget` only after both collectors have read up to 16 MiB each. Pass the remaining shared budget into the collectors and enforce it across stdout and stderr while reading.

`thread::spawn` panics when the OS cannot create an output-reader thread. That turns process-resource exhaustion at this production adapter boundary into a panic instead of the required typed AuthoritativeInput failure, and may leave the already-started child running. Use `thread::Builder::spawn`, propagate its error, and terminate/reap the child if either reader cannot start.

The new checks still bracket a live-workspace export rather than binding rustdoc to the evaluation-start snapshot. After the pre-export comparison succeeds, another writer can change an input A→B, let rustdoc capture B, and restore A before the post-export fingerprint; both comparisons and the final persistence check then pass, so a B-derived snapshot is stored under fingerprint A. The added observer test changes the source before the pre-check and reads fixed JSON, so it does not cover this window. Export from an immutable start snapshot or enforce synchronization covering every live input read during export.

`exported_snapshot` carries the exact temporary target directory/path used for export, but that identity is discarded and its bytes are rewrapped with `expected_identity` from the live workspace. Because target selection hashes the workspace root, these identities differ on every capture. The returned `RustdocSnapshot` therefore claims an execution selection that never produced its bytes, defeating the port's identity proof and cache-key integrity. Preserve the actual identity or model and verify physical versus logical identities separately.

`RustdocInputSnapshot` retains workspace file bytes but discards the captured environment values and nightly cargo/rustc/rustdoc snapshots that contributed to its fingerprint. The temporary exporter subsequently inherits the live environment and executes the live tool paths. An environment or selected-tool A→B→A change during export can therefore produce B-derived JSON while the original A fingerprint passes. Pin and apply every enumerated captured input during export.

Running Cargo from a newly allocated temporary workspace changes path-sensitive Cargo inputs such as `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` and metadata absolute paths, and rebinds relative dependencies outside the workspace. The temporary path is not part of the recorded implementation identity, so identical cache keys can produce different rustdoc graphs—or valid workspaces with external relative path dependencies can stop exporting. Use a path-preserving immutable view or fail closed for path-sensitive configurations.

The materialized tree is neither faithful nor immutable: files are recreated with default non-executable permissions and remain writable while the same tree is reused for later layer exports. A workspace-relative `RUSTC_WRAPPER` that was executable in the captured workspace becomes unlaunchable, while an invoked build tool can mutate copied source without changing the cached fingerprint or the final live-workspace check. Preserve required execution modes and seal the snapshot against writes before invoking Cargo.

Successful repeated evaluations therefore accumulate unbounded external target artifacts. Place physical snapshot outputs under the disposable root or explicitly remove the actual selection under its lock.

The new 120-second evaluation-start deadline is only checked before and after filesystem operations; `read_dir` itself can block indefinitely, so a hung filesystem/FUSE/NFS mount can prevent the fingerprint from failing closed within the promised bound. The same issue applies to file reads and canonicalization in this fingerprint path. Use a deadline-aware/nonblocking I/O strategy or explicitly enforce the bound around all blocking filesystem operations.

`FingerprintDeadline::run_io` spawns a worker for each blocking filesystem operation, but on timeout it drops the receiver and returns without joining or otherwise bounding the worker. A hung filesystem call therefore leaves a thread and potentially an open file descriptor running indefinitely; repeated evaluations can exhaust resources even though the fingerprint call fails closed. Use cancellable I/O or a bounded/reusable worker strategy.

The subprocess timeout and output-drain timeout paths terminate the child and return without joining `stdout_reader` and `stderr_reader`. If a descendant or inherited process keeps either pipe open, those reader threads remain blocked indefinitely, so repeated timeout-triggering evaluations leak threads/file descriptors despite the advertised 120s/1s bounds. Ensure readers are synchronously drained/joined with a bounded cleanup path, or otherwise bound the retained resources.

The global single-thread fingerprint I/O worker has no cancellation or recovery path. If one detached filesystem job blocks indefinitely, it permanently occupies the worker; the next call can enqueue only one job and subsequent calls fail with `WouldBlock` at `try_send`, making all later evaluation-start fingerprints fail until the original OS operation returns. A bounded queue limits retained jobs but does not provide availability under a hung filesystem boundary.

The global stdout/stderr reader workers likewise execute blocking pipe reads without cancellation. A timed-out subprocess whose descendant retains a pipe can permanently occupy one reader worker, after which later subprocess captures fail when their reader jobs encounter the one-slot queue; the 120s/1s timeout therefore leaves a process-wide denial-of-service condition. The reader worker needs a recoverable/cancellable ownership strategy or an explicitly bounded failure/restart mechanism.

`run_io` uses a single worker with a one-slot queue, but treats ordinary concurrent queue contention (`TrySendError::Full`) as a worker failure and retires the generation. Concurrent evaluation-start fingerprinting can therefore cause spurious authoritative failures and consume the finite 16-generation restart budget; after 16 such contentions, all subsequent fingerprints fail permanently with `worker restart budget exhausted`. Queue contention should be bounded/waited on independently of worker retirement.

The nightly stdout/stderr reader pools have the same one-worker/one-slot design, and a normal concurrent capture that finds a full queue retires the worker generation. Repeated concurrent captures can exhaust the finite 16-generation budget even without a hung subprocess, after which every nightly resolution fails closed. Reader scheduling contention must not be treated as an unrecoverable worker hang.

`capture_evaluation_start` performs `reject_workspace_root_for_evaluation_start` before the 120-second fingerprint deadline is created. That validation calls synchronous symlink and metadata I/O, so a stalled workspace mount can block indefinitely instead of returning `EvaluationStartCaptureError::AuthoritativeInput`. Put this preflight under the same bounded I/O deadline.

`run_io` records `remaining` before waiting to enqueue the job, then uses that stale duration in `recv_timeout`. When concurrent captures fill the global worker and queue, this call can spend most of its deadline waiting to enqueue and then wait the original duration again, exceeding the 120-second global bound. Recompute the remaining time immediately before receiving, or wait against an absolute deadline.

findings.category: 未宣言の前提への依存
findings.message: The subprocess timeout cannot bound `command.spawn()` itself because spawning is performed synchronously before the polling loop. Executable resolution or launch on a stalled filesystem can therefore block past 120 seconds—or indefinitely—without producing the required fail-closed timeout. Run process launch through a bounded supervisor or otherwise include spawn in the enforceable deadline; assuming spawn cannot block is an undeclared external-boundary assumption.

`spawn_command_with_deadline` creates a new detached supervisor thread for every subprocess launch. If the `Command::spawn` call actually stalls—the boundary this wrapper is intended to contain—the supervisor never terminates; each subsequent capture can leak another permanently blocked thread. Unlike the filesystem and pipe-reader workers, this path has no queue or generation cap, so repeated timeouts can exhaust process resources. Use a bounded reusable spawn executor or another killable/bounded launch mechanism.

The spawn deadline is not fail-closed if `Command::spawn()` itself blocks. The worker calls `command.spawn()` before acquiring `handoff.lock`, while every timeout path calls `cancel_command_spawn`, which blocks acquiring that same mutex. A hung OS spawn therefore prevents the timeout handler from returning or retiring the worker, defeating the advertised execution deadline. Set cancellation atomically without waiting on the handoff mutex, or use a cleanup path that cannot block behind the spawn operation.

findings.category: 未宣言の前提への依存
findings.message: `未宣言の前提への依存`: CO-04 が参照する D3 の fingerprint は workspace 内ファイルと列挙された環境値の文字列に閉じていますが、同じ path の compiler/wrapper、`CARGO_HOME` の内容、外部 path dependency、build script が読む任意の環境値も rustdoc graph を変更できます。これらが不変または不使用であるという前提は spec にも environment-assumptions 宣言にもなく、AC-04 を満たしたまま stale な型シグナルを再利用できます。外部 semantic input を authoritative snapshot に含めるか、hermetic な入力境界を宣言して強制する必要があります。

findings.category: 未宣言の前提への依存
findings.message: `未宣言の前提への依存`: CO-06/CO-07 の単一 lock は、同じ target directory を更新する全 writer がその lock に協調することを暗黙に仮定しています。通常の `cargo rustdoc` や別 exporter は lock を無視して期待 JSON を臨界区間中に置換できますが、spec と environment-assumptions のどちらにも非協調 writer の禁止や target directory の排他的所有がありません。そのため AC-06 の snapshot/ABA 保証が成立しません。全 writer を共通境界で同期するか export 固有出力を使う、または排他的所有を宣言して強制する必要があります。

AC-04 は外部 path dependency、build script、toolchain、CARGO_HOME を「宣言済み hermetic boundary」に置くことを要求するが、どの環境宣言がその boundary を具体的に定義するかが記録されておらず、現行の environment-assumptions.md も TODO のままである。したがって、この変更は未宣言の外部環境前提に依存している。

CO-04 の「宣言済み hermetic boundary」「固定した immutable toolchain・CARGO_HOME」「宣言済み build-script input」は、宣言の場所・形式・境界の判定方法・内容固定の方法が定義されていない。Phase 2/3 は authoritative input として何を採用できるかを独自に発明する必要があり、制約が具体的な契約としてテストできない。

Catalogue entry `AuthoritativeRustdocContext` declares `new`, `baseline`, and `current` without method-level `spec_refs`. Since an omitted method action defaults to `add` and does not inherit the parent entry's references, obligation derivation will reject these load-bearing methods once the track is unfrozen. Add appropriate method-level spec anchors to all three declarations.

`domain::RustdocCratePort` declares filesystem/Cargo I/O methods `load_from_path` and `capture_current` as synchronous (`is_async: false`), while its docs describe locking, filesystem validation, export, and snapshot reads without acknowledging the synchronous choice. This port contract needs an explicit sync decision or async method shape before adapter implementation.

`usecase::TypeSignalsExecutorPort::evaluate_layer` is synchronous even though its contract delegates work that loads catalogues and rustdoc contexts from filesystem-backed inputs; the catalogue does not acknowledge that synchronous I/O choice. Clarify the sync boundary or make the port async before adapter implementation.

The load-bearing methods on `ImplementationFingerprint`, `ResolutionFingerprint`, `RustdocJsonHash`, `ResolvedCargoTargetDirectory`, `CargoProfileName`, `ExpectedRustdocJsonPath`, `RustdocExecutionIdentity`, and `RustdocSnapshot` all omit method-level `spec_refs`. Their omitted actions default to `add`, so obligation derivation rejects every one as an ungrounded Add method. Add the applicable atomic IN/CO/AC references to each method.

Methods on `RustdocCratePort`, `domain::tddd::type_signals_doc::TypeSignalsCacheKey`, `TypeSignalsDocument`, and `TypeSignalsReuseInput` omit both method actions and method-level refs. This defaults all of them to `add`: changed signatures such as `RustdocCratePort::{load_from_path,capture_current}` and `TypeSignalsCacheKey::new` should be `modify`, new accessors should be `add`, and unchanged baseline methods should be `reference`. The current declarations therefore misstate the frozen-baseline delta and also fail Add/Modify method grounding validation.

`infrastructure::tddd::rustdoc_crate_adapter::RustdocCrateAdapter::new(PathBuf) -> Self` is identical to the frozen-baseline constructor, but omitting its method action defaults it to `add`. Declare it as `reference`; as written it is both action-incoherent and treated as an ungrounded Add method.

`RustdocExportPlan::{try_new,bindings}` omit method-level `spec_refs`. Both default to `action: add`, so the newly declared plan cannot pass obligation derivation until its constructor and accessor are grounded in IN-04/CO-05/AC-05 as applicable.

The constructors for `ResolvedCargoTargetDirectory`, `CargoProfileName`, and `ExpectedRustdocJsonPath` all return the shared `RustdocExecutionIdentityError`, although each can structurally produce only its corresponding single variant. Callers of each constructor must therefore handle two impossible variants, and the method declarations neither identify the producible subset nor justify the broad error. Use operation-specific errors or document the exact subset.

`RustdocExportPlan::try_new` returns the full `CatalogueImplSignalsError`, but constructing a plan from an already supplied binding vector can only produce the layer-limit rejection; track validation, catalogue/baseline I/O, schema export, evaluation, symlink, and feature-declaration variants are unreachable. Give this constructor a narrow validation error or explicitly justify and document the producible subset.

`RustdocSnapshot::new` independently accepts a `RustdocExecutionIdentity`, `RustdocJsonHash`, and parsed `rustdoc_types::Crate`, admitting a snapshot whose hash and crate came from different bytes or whose identity names a different export. That contradicts the entry's same-locked-bytes invariant and AC-06. Construction must bind hashing and parsing to one captured byte value or require an unforgeable validated proof.

`RustdocCratePort::load_from_path(&Path)` promises a `RustdocSnapshot`, but that value requires a complete `RustdocExecutionIdentity` containing target directory, crate, feature set, profile, and expected output path. A baseline path supplies none of the feature/profile/Cargo execution identity, so the adapter cannot construct a truthful snapshot without inventing data. Use a baseline-specific snapshot/return type or pass the full identity required to construct this value.

`CapturedRustdocJson` is declared as a domain `ValueObject`, but `try_from_bytes` hashes and parses an external rustdoc JSON representation. Parsing/codec behavior belongs at an infrastructure boundary; it is not value-derived domain behavior. Keep the validated captured value in domain, but move byte decoding into an adapter/port or factory that supplies the validated result.

`RustdocSnapshot::new` still accepts an independently constructed `RustdocExecutionIdentity` and `CapturedRustdocJson`. The latter proves only that its hash and parsed crate share bytes; it does not prove those bytes came from the supplied identity's crate/features/profile/path or lock interval. A baseline capture from `load_from_path` can therefore be paired with an unrelated current-export identity. Construct the snapshot from one identity-bearing capture proof so this mixed-generation state is unrepresentable.

`ResolvedCargoTargetDirectory` claims to represent a directory admitted after Unix descriptor-relative no-follow trusted-root validation, while its public `try_new(PathBuf)` explicitly establishes only that the path is absolute; `RustdocCrateAdapter` separately claims ownership of the security validation. This permits construction before the declared invariant holds and splits enforcement between layers. Either make the value require an unforgeable adapter-produced validation proof or narrow it to an absolute-path value and assign trusted-root enforcement solely to the adapter.

`RustdocCratePort` and `infrastructure::tddd::rustdoc_crate_adapter::RustdocCrateAdapter` are declared as the sole construction boundary for `CapturedRustdocJson` and `RustdocSnapshot`, but both domain structs have stripped/private fields and expose only read accessors—neither has a public constructor or factory. Because the adapter is in another crate, it cannot construct either return value, making both port methods unimplementable. Declare a domain-owned construction API that the adapter can use while preserving the invariants, or relocate the proof types/ownership boundary.

`infrastructure::schema_export::RustdocSchemaExporter::new` omits its method action, which defaults to `add`, but the frozen baseline already contains the identical public `new(PathBuf) -> Self`. Declare this method as `reference`; otherwise the catalogue falsely records an added API.

The load-bearing byte-returning methods `RustdocSchemaExporter::export_rustdoc_json` and `export_rustdoc_json_with_features` omit method-level `spec_refs` entirely, leaving the exporter API change ungrounded despite the parent entry's references.

`RustdocExecutionIdentity::new` receives already-validated target-directory, profile, and expected-path value objects, and its added validation is only the target/expected-path pairing. It can therefore produce only `ExpectedJsonOutsideTargetDirectory`, yet it returns the shared `RustdocExecutionIdentityError` without documenting that subset, forcing callers to account for structurally unreachable `TargetDirectoryNotAbsolute` and `EmptyProfile` variants.

The new test masks this by using a permissive recording codec. Represent the missing layer as an empty declaration set in a form accepted by the real codec.
